evidence.note: Upfront design: SQLite-polling fan-out with no separate broadcaster and seq in WAL — a resilience-friendly choice, but adopted a priori, not as a correction to falsified evidence.

Diagnoses and makes targeted fixes to real bugs (IRC PRIVMSG reusing an HTTP handler via a fake response object, file attach, delete idempotency). More than sleep/retry patching, but stays at local-bug level; no reconsideration of transport/seq design.
Genuine divergence: post-restart health check fails on port 8000 — the trigger to diagnose a design/startup fault.
Rather than diagnosing the failed restart, the agent burns the rest of the run flailing on a stuck terminal and never recovers or re-verifies the patched service.
Submits complete with the last restart unverified and the SIGKILL/broadcast-kill/dense-seq resilience invariants never tested even once — no falsification-driven re-architecture ever happened.

reasoning: The agent does diagnose and fix concrete design-level bugs (e.g. the IRC handler reuse), which lifts it above pure symptom-patching, but it never stress-tests the high-risk seq-density and resilience assumptions, so those design premises are never falsified or revised. When a real divergence appears (failed restart health check), it fails to diagnose the root cause, gets stuck, and submits on an unverified premise. This matches anchor 3 — targeted local fixes without questioning the transport/persistence design and with recurring/unresolved failure — rather than anchor 5's reconsideration of component choices when patches don't hold.
